raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

This PR is stacked on #63386 (GLM-5.3 latency-specialized decode). Until that PR lands, this branch also contains its commit; only the last commit is under review.

With `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'`, the GLM-5.3 MTP draft layer (layer 78) moves off vLLM's stock DeepSeek-V3.2 MTP path onto CuTe DSL kernels (draft worker, draft selectors, MoE, BF16 draft head, MTP preprocess). The draft layer reads vLLM's loaded MTP-layer weights in place.

The PR also changes Model Runner V2 for low-batch speculative decode. These paths are taken only when a model state sets `ModelState.low_latency_decode` (default `False`). Only `Glm53ModelState` sets it, so every other model runs Model Runner V2 unchanged.

**Revision 2** (this push). Compared with revision 1:
- the drafter serves MTP K = 1 to 7 and batches of up to four requests (revision 1: one request at K = 3);
- the Model Runner V2 paths are enabled by the model state's `low_latency_decode` attribute; the `VLLM_POST_FORWARD_CUDA_GRAPH` environment variable is removed;
- it passes the repository's pre-commit hooks and mypy;
- it is rebased on current main and on revision 2 of #63386.

## Claims

- MTP 3 at an 8K prompt with synthetic acceptance length 2.99: lower TPOT than stock at 1, 2 and 4 requests (about -52%, -33% and -18%). MTP 1 at one request: about -49%. These numbers include the target-layer change from #63386; table below.
- GSM8K is within noise of stock: 0.923 vs 0.902 at MTP 3, 0.911 vs 0.913 at MTP off.
- Long-context and reasoning evals at MTP 3 match stock within their standard errors where both arms have finished (RULER, MRCR); GPQA and AIME stock arms are still running.
- In the runs below, no claimed decode step fell back to the stock forward after startup, and no kernel compiled at request time.
- Without the opt-in, Model Runner V2 behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

All runs on 8xB200. Stock = upstream main (the parent of #63386's commit) with no additional config; this change adds `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'`.

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --block-size 64 \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": K, "use_local_argmax_reduction": true}' \
  --max-num-seqs S [--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}']
```

### Tests

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/glm53                     # one B200: 644 passed
pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_low_batch_spec_decode.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_eplb.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py
  # 109 passed
```

The Model Runner V2 tests include a check that a model state without the opt-in creates no post-forward graph.

### Accuracy

**GSM8K**, all 1,319 questions, 5-shot, T = 0, served (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`), natural acceptance.

| Config | Stock | This change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MTP 3, `--max-num-seqs 4`, concurrency 4 | 0.902 | 0.923 |
| MTP 1, `--max-num-seqs 8`, concurrency 8 | - | 0.913 |
| MTP off, `--max-num-seqs 16`, concurrency 16 | 0.913 | 0.911 |

**Long-context and reasoning, MTP 3** (in progress; `--max-model-len 540672`, no prefix caching, `--max-num-seqs 4`, natural acceptance, same flags in both arms):

| Task | Samples | Stock | This change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GPQA-Diamond (reasoning effort high, T = 0.6, top-p 0.95, 64K output cap) | 198 × 16 seeds | running | 67.96 (SE 2.21) |
| AIME25 (T = 0.6, 64K output cap) | 30 × 16 seeds | running | 84.17 (SE 4.12) |
| MRCR v2, 8-needle, 128K to 256K | 100 | 40.54 (SE 3.87) | 43.50 (SE 3.86); delta +2.96 (SE 5.47) |
| RULER `niah_single_2` / `niah_multikey_2` / `niah_multikey_3` at 32K / 128K / 256K / 512K | 40 per cell | 100 in every cell except `niah_multikey_2` 256K (97.5) | 100 in every cell |

RULER tasks (lm-eval `ruler` group): `niah_single_2` hides one key-value needle in essay text; `niah_multikey_2` fills the whole context with key-value needles and asks for one key; `niah_multikey_3` does the same with UUID keys and values. A GPQA or AIME answer truncated at the 64K cap counts as wrong (this change: 309 of 3,168 GPQA and 50 of 480 AIME answers). These evals ran on an earlier build of this revision; later changes touch only startup checks, imports and tests. This table will be updated when the stock arms finish.

### Speed, MTP on

TPOT on the served path, 8K prompt, 1,536 output tokens, B concurrent requests. MTP uses synthetic acceptance (`"rejection_sample_method": "synthetic"`) with acceptance length 2.99 at MTP 3 and 1.84 at MTP 1, so both arms accept the same number of tokens per step. Three server restarts per arm, alternating stock and this change; median and range.

| MTP | B | TPOT, stock (ms) | TPOT, this change (ms) | Change | Step p50, stock / this (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | 1 | 3.313 [3.308-3.322] | 1.601 [1.594-1.617] | -51.7% | 9.873 / 4.783 |
| 3 | 2 | 3.862 [3.859-3.864] | 2.586 [2.568-2.589] | -33.0% | 11.560 / 7.745 |
| 3 | 4 | 4.541 [4.535-4.578] | 3.745 [3.741-3.770] | -17.5% | 13.590 / 11.219 |
| 1 | 1 | 4.807 [4.758-4.815] | 2.452 [2.451-2.459] | -49.0% | 8.900 / 4.537 |

The stock arm runs vLLM's target layers and vLLM's drafter; this change runs #63386's target layers and this PR's drafter.

## Details

**Design.**
- Drafter: the catch-up holds four rows per request (one padded window at K = 1 and 2, two windows at K = 4 to 7). Request tiers of up to four requests at K = 2 and 3, and up to two at K = 1 and 4 to 7, run the drafter beside the target's row tiers. Any other step runs vLLM's drafter.
- At K = 1, where vLLM compacts no top-k indices, the model state's postprocess hook gives the drafter its sampled rows.
- The target segment caches the attention metadata of steps whose graphs it and the drafter fully claim.

**Model Runner V2 changes** (only with `ModelState.low_latency_decode` and an MTP/EAGLE drafter on CUDA):
- one post-forward CUDA graph per uniform decode size: sampling, state update and draft-prefill inputs after each step (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/post_forward_cudagraph.py`);
- fused draft-prefill stores;
- draft decodes that the model state claims (`ModelState.claims_draft_decode_capture`) store their drafts inside the graph;
- kernel copies inside captures.

These are attributes and branches on the existing speculator and graph classes. A state that opts in must keep `postprocess_state` safe to capture in a CUDA graph. Pipeline parallelism, context parallelism and other unsupported configurations fall back to the baseline path with a warning.

**Requirements and limits.** Those of #63386, plus: MTP needs `"use_local_argmax_reduction": true`. The drafter's request tiers add capture sizes 1 and 2 at MTP 3. Draft activations stay BF16 where the stock drafter quantizes them to FP8, so individual draft tokens can differ from the stock drafter's.

**Overlap.** #61869 (DeepSeek-V4.1) adds its own `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/post_forward_cudagraph.py`; whichever lands first, the other will build on it. The Kimi K3 (`vllm/models/kimi_k3`) and DeepSeek-V4.1 (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41`) specialized paths serve other architectures and do not specialize the MTP drafter.

**CI.** `pytest -v -s models/glm53` runs in #63386's B200 step (`glm53-unit-tests-b200`); the Model Runner V2 tests in `tests/v1/worker` run in the existing worker steps. The served TP8 path needs a full 8-GPU node and is validated outside CI.

**AI assistance.** AI coding assistants (Claude) were used to write this change and run its validation; the submitter reviewed every changed line. Commits carry a `Co-authored-by` trailer.


---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [ ] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The decode segment's guards for block-table entries its padding rows index."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.decode import kernel_block_table, null_padding_block
+
+BLOCK = 64
+ROWS = 4
+KEY_TILE = 128
+
+
+def _kernel_entries(position: int, rows: int) -> list[int]:
+    last = (position + rows - 1) // BLOCK
+    return list(range(position // BLOCK, last + 2))
+
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""GLM-5.3 CuTe DSL kernel families
+(vllm/models/glm53/nvidia/ops/cute_dsl), on a GPU.
+"""
+
+import importlib.util
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.ops.cute_dsl import registry
+
+HIDDEN, VOCAB, SHARD_ROWS = 6144, 154880, 19360
+ROPE_CAPACITY = 16384
+
+
+def _sm100() -> bool:
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] != 10:
+        return False
+    return importlib.util.find_spec("cutlass") is not None
+
+
+sm100 = pytest.mark.skipif(not _sm100(), reason="needs an SM100 GPU and CuTe DSL")
+
+
+def _inputs() -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    embedding = torch.randn(VOCAB, HIDDEN, device=device).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    specials = torch.tensor(
+        [0x7FC1, -127, 0x7F80, -128, 0x0001, -32767, 0, -32768], dtype=torch.int16
+    )
+    embedding.view(torch.int16)[VOCAB - 1, :8] = specials.to(device)
+    tokens = torch.tensor([VOCAB - 1, 0, SHARD_ROWS - 1, 77777], dtype=torch.int32)
+    return {
+        "embedding": embedding,
+        "token_ids": tokens.to(device),
+        "position": torch.tensor([12345], dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        "rope": torch.randn(ROPE_CAPACITY, 64, device=device),
+        # The q4 row table: R = 4 live rows of B = 1 request starting at row 0.
+        "row_table": torch.tensor(
+            [4, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        ),
+        # The one-row build's table (the drafter's proposals): R = 1 live row.
+        "row_table_q1": torch.tensor(
+            [1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0], dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        ),
+    }
+
+
+def _outputs() -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    out = {
+        "hidden_q4": torch.empty(4, HIDDEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device),
+        "freq_q4": torch.empty(4, 64, device=device),
+        "hidden_v1": torch.empty(4, HIDDEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device),
+        "freq_v1": torch.empty(4, 64, device=device),
+        "hidden_v4": torch.empty(4, HIDDEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device),
+        "freq_v4": torch.empty(4, 64, device=device),
+    }
+    for tensor in out.values():
+        tensor.view(torch.uint8).fill_(0xA5)
+    return out
+
+
+def _launches(x, out) -> None:
+    from cuda.bindings.driver import CUstream
+
+    device = torch.accelerator.current_device_index()
+    stream = CUstream(torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream)
+
+    def launch(name: str, values: list) -> None:
+        registry.executor(name, device)(*registry.bind(name, values), stream)
+
+    shards = [x["embedding"].data_ptr() + p * SHARD_ROWS * HIDDEN * 2 for p in range(8)]
+    common = [x["token_ids"].data_ptr(), x["position"].data_ptr()]
+    launch(
+        "prologue_q4",
+        [
+            *common,
+            x["embedding"].data_ptr(),
+            x["rope"].data_ptr(),
+            out["hidden_q4"].data_ptr(),
+            out["freq_q4"].data_ptr(),
+            ROPE_CAPACITY,
+            x["row_table"].data_ptr(),
+        ],
+    )
+    for name, tag, table in (
+        ("prologue_vllm", "v1", "row_table_q1"),
+        ("prologue_vllm_q4", "v4", "row_table"),
+    ):
+        launch(
+            name,
+            [
+                *common,
+                x["rope"].data_ptr(),
+                out[f"hidden_{tag}"].data_ptr(),
+                out[f"freq_{tag}"].data_ptr(),
+                ROPE_CAPACITY,
+                x[table].data_ptr(),
+                *shards,
+            ],
+        )
+
+
+def _programmatic_edges(graph: torch.cuda.CUDAGraph) -> int:
+    from cuda.bindings import driver
+
+    handle = driver.CUgraph(graph.raw_cuda_graph())
+    error, _, _, _, count = driver.cuGraphGetEdges(handle, 0)
+    assert int(error) == 0, error
+    error, _, _, data, count = driver.cuGraphGetEdges(handle, count)
+    assert int(error) == 0, error
+    programmatic = driver.CUgraphDependencyType.CU_GRAPH_DEPENDENCY_TYPE_PROGRAMMATIC
+    return sum(1 for edge in data[:count] if edge.type == programmatic)
+
+
+@sm100
+def test_cute_entries_build_and_bind():
+    device = torch.accelerator.current_device_index()
+    for name in registry.ENTRIES:
+        assert registry.executor(name, device) is registry.executor(name, device), name
+
+
+CHAINED = ("prologue_q4", "prologue_vllm", "prologue_vllm_q4")
+
+
+@sm100
+def test_cute_entries_replay_bitwise_in_a_pdl_graph():
+    x = _inputs()
+    out = _outputs()
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        _launches(x, out)
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    eager = {k: v.clone() for k, v in out.items()}
+    for tensor in out.values():
+        tensor.view(torch.uint8).fill_(0xA5)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph(keep_graph=True)
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        _launches(x, out)
+    assert _programmatic_edges(graph) == len(CHAINED) - 1
+    graph.instantiate()
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    for key in out:
+        assert torch.equal(out[key].view(torch.uint8), eager[key].view(torch.uint8)), (
+            key
+        )

+"""The drafter's step-word kernels, per request of a tier."""

+import pytest

+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU")
+
+T = 4
+WIDTH = 1024
+
+
+def _table(live: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.tensor([T * live, live, 0, 0], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+
+def _words(requests: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    return (
+        torch.zeros(2 * T * requests, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        torch.zeros(requests, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        torch.ones(2 * requests, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("requests", "live"), [(1, 1), (4, 3), (12, 12)])
+def test_a_captured_catchup_counts_a_generation_and_sets_the_live_words(requests, live):
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    positions = torch.zeros(T * requests, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    positions[::T] = 100 * torch.arange(1, requests + 1, device=device)
+    accepts = [(b + 1) % T for b in range(requests)]
+    last = torch.tensor(
+        [T * b + accepts[b] for b in range(requests)], dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+    )
+    position, accepted, context = _words(requests)
+    for _ in range(3):
+        glm53_draft._catchup_words_kernel[(requests,)](
+            positions, last, _table(live), position, accepted, context, T=T
+        )
+    for b in range(requests):
+        if b < live:
+            assert position[2 * T * b].item() == 100 * (b + 1)
+            assert accepted[b].item() == accepts[b]
+            assert context[2 * b : 2 * b + 2].tolist() == [
+                100 * (b + 1) + accepts[b] + 1,
+                4,
+            ]
+        else:
+            assert position[2 * T * b].item() == 0 and accepted[b].item() == 0
+            assert context[2 * b : 2 * b + 2].tolist() == [1, 1]
+    # The positions are an int64-style array: only each first row's low word is set.
+    assert position.view(-1, 2 * T)[:, 1:].count_nonzero().item() == 0
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("starts", "lasts"),

+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    tokens = max(lasts) + 1
+    idle = [0] * (requests - live)
+    last = torch.tensor(lasts + idle, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    query_start_loc = torch.tensor(
+        starts + [tokens] * (requests + 1 - live), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+    )
+    positions = torch.arange(tokens, dtype=torch.int64, device=device) + 50
+    token_ids = torch.arange(tokens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    rows = torch.randn(tokens, WIDTH, device=device).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    rows_scratch = torch.zeros(T * requests, WIDTH, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+    token_scratch = torch.zeros(T * requests, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    position, accepted, context = _words(requests)
+    glm53_draft._gather_inputs_kernel[(WIDTH // 1024, requests)](
+        last,
+        query_start_loc,
+        positions,
+        token_ids,
+        rows,
+        token_scratch,
+        rows_scratch,
+        position,
+        accepted,
+        context,
+        _table(live),
+        tokens,

+        WIDTH=WIDTH,

+        first = lasts[b] - a

+        assert position[2 * T * b].item() == 50 + first
+        assert context[2 * b : 2 * b + 2].tolist() == [50 + first + a + 1, 2]
+        for i in range(a + 1):
+            assert torch.equal(rows_scratch[T * b + i], rows[first + i])
+            assert token_scratch[T * b + i].item() == first + i

+def _stage(drafts: int, window: int, positions: list[int], accepts: list[int]):
+    """Stage one window of ``len(positions)`` live requests of a tier of four; return
+    the staged tensors, vLLM's source rows and the block table before the step.
+    """
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    requests, live, rows_per = 4, len(positions), drafts + 1
+    tokens = torch.arange(rows_per * requests, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) + 9
+    rows = torch.randn(rows_per * requests, WIDTH, device=device).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    blocks = torch.arange(1, 1 + requests * 64, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)

+        ),
+        "draft.t.accept": torch.zeros(requests, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        "token_ids": torch.zeros(4 * requests, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),

+        "position": torch.zeros(8 * requests, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),

+    before = blocks.clone()
+    table = torch.tensor([4 * live, live, 0, 0], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)

+    )
+    return tensors, tokens, rows, before.view(requests, 64)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("drafts", [1, 2])

+    tensors, _, _, before = _stage(drafts, 1, [position, position], [0, 0])
+    after = tensors[glm53_draft.BLOCK_TABLE]
+    expected = before.clone()
+    if nulled is not None:
+        expected[:2, nulled] = 0  # both live requests, not the idle ones
+    assert torch.equal(after, expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("window", [0, 1])
+def test_two_windows_take_four_true_rows_and_null_no_block(window):

+    assert tensors["position"][0].item() == position + start
+    assert tensors["mtp.accept"][0].item() == (0 if window == 0 else 1)
+    assert torch.equal(tensors[glm53_draft.BLOCK_TABLE], before)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""GLM-5.3 kernel registry and launch program, on the CPU."""
+
+import struct
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia import draft_providers, providers, switch
+from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.ops import launch as glm53_launch
+from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.ops.cute_dsl.mla_selector import IndexScale, StateWords
+from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.ops.cute_dsl.mla_worker import Handoff, MlaWorker
+
+
+class _AnyTensors(dict):
+    """Every input resolves to a small CPU tensor (the target providers); no replicated
+    embedding.
+    """
+
+    def __missing__(self, name: str) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if name == glm53_launch.BLOCK_TABLE:
+            tensor = torch.zeros(16384 // 64, dtype=torch.int32)
+        elif name == "rope_table":
+            tensor = torch.zeros(16384, 64)
+        else:
+            tensor = torch.zeros(8, dtype=torch.int32)
+        self[name] = tensor
+        return tensor
+
+    def __contains__(self, name: object) -> bool:
+        return name != "embedding"
+
+
+class _ReplicatedEmbedding(_AnyTensors):
+    """A replicated ``embedding`` table instead of vLLM's shards."""
+
+    def __contains__(self, name: object) -> bool:
+        return True
+
+
+class _Placement:
+    """CPU stand-in for ``Glm53Placement``: plain handoff and flags (``issued``: the
+    ``moe_flags`` pairs handed out, in order).
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.issued: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = []
+
+    def worker_handoff(self, by_sm: bool, groups: int = 1) -> SimpleNamespace:
+        return SimpleNamespace(
+            handoff=torch.zeros(groups * Handoff.WORDS, dtype=torch.int32),
+            mirror=torch.zeros(groups * Handoff.WORDS, dtype=torch.int32),
+        )
+
+    def moe_flags(self, rows: int = 4) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        words = glm53_launch.sizes_of(f"fused_moe_q{rows}_ckpt_shared")["kFlagWords"]
+        pair = (
+            torch.zeros(words, dtype=torch.int32),
+            torch.zeros(words, dtype=torch.int32),
+        )
+        self.issued.append(pair)
+        return pair
+
+
+def _bound(program: Sequence[providers.Provider]) -> list[glm53_launch.Launch]:
+    launches = []
+    for provider in program:
+        provider.bind(lambda name: [peer << 40 for peer in range(8)])
+        assert provider.launch is not None
+        launches.append(provider.launch)
+    return launches
+
+
+def _deployment_geometries(
+    shape: glm53_launch.Glm53Geometry,
+) -> list[glm53_launch.Glm53Geometry]:
+    geometries: list[glm53_launch.Glm53Geometry] = []
+    for per_request in range(1, 9):
+        for requests in range(1, switch.MAX_REQUESTS + 1):
+            if not switch.serves_shape(requests, per_request):
+                continue
+            tier = switch.shape_tier(requests, per_request)
+            packed = switch.packed_tier(tier, per_request)
+            rows = per_request if packed else switch.lone_rows(per_request)
+            w8a16 = switch.shape_w8a16_rows(requests, per_request)
+            live = 0 if packed else per_request
+            geometry = shape.for_tier(tier, rows - 1, packed, w8a16, live)
+            if geometry in geometries:
+                continue
+            geometries.append(geometry)
+    return geometries
+
+
+def test_shipped_kernels_are_the_served_kernels(geometry) -> None:
+    from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.ops.cute_dsl import registry
+
+    launched: list[glm53_launch.Launch] = []

+def test_index_scale_words() -> None:

+
+    for exponent in range(1, 255):
+        scale = struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<I", exponent << 23))[0]
+        assert scale == 2.0 ** (exponent - 127)
+        packed = ((exponent << 23) >> 23 & 0xFF) * 0x01010101
+        assert int(IndexScale.word(Uint32(exponent))) == packed
+        decoded = struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<I", (packed & 255) << 23))[0]
+        assert decoded == scale

+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import threading
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia import kv as glm53_kv
+from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.kv import Glm53KvHygiene, PendingRows, Rows
+
+BLOCK = 64
+BLOCKS = 6
+WORLD = 8
+
+
+def make_caches(layers: int, seed: int) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    """One block-outer buffer holding every layer's MLA and index pages, as vLLM's
+    views.
+    """
+    page_mla, page_index = BLOCK * 576, BLOCK * 132
+    stride = layers * (page_mla + page_index)
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    buffer = torch.randint(
+        0, 256, (BLOCKS * stride,), dtype=torch.uint8, generator=generator
+    )
+    caches = {}
+    for layer in range(layers):
+        base = layer * (page_mla + page_index)
+        caches[f"model.layers.{layer}.self_attn.attn"] = torch.as_strided(
+            buffer, (BLOCKS, BLOCK, 576), (stride, 576, 1), base
+        )
+        caches[f"model.layers.{layer}.self_attn.indexer.k_cache"] = torch.as_strided(
+            buffer, (BLOCKS, BLOCK, 132), (stride, 132, 1), base + page_mla
+        )
+    return caches
+
+
+class Group:
+    """One rank's handle on a simulated TP group (threads, one per rank)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, shared: dict, rank: int) -> None:
+        self.shared, self.rank_in_group, self.world_size = shared, rank, WORLD
+
+    def broadcast(self, input_: torch.Tensor, src: int = 0) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if self.rank_in_group == src:
+            self.shared["data"] = input_.clone()
+        self.shared["barrier"].wait()
+        input_.copy_(self.shared["data"])
+        self.shared["barrier"].wait()
+        return input_
+
+
+def run_ranks(work) -> list:
+    """Run ``work(rank, group)`` on eight threads; return the per-rank results."""
+    shared = {"barrier": threading.Barrier(WORLD)}
+    results: list = [None] * WORLD
+    errors: list[BaseException] = []
+
+    def body(rank: int) -> None:
+        try:
+            results[rank] = work(rank, Group(shared, rank))
+        except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - reported below
+            errors.append(error)
+            shared["barrier"].abort()
+
+    threads = [threading.Thread(target=body, args=(rank,)) for rank in range(WORLD)]
+    for thread in threads:
+        thread.start()
+    for thread in threads:
+        thread.join()
+    if errors:
+        raise errors[0]
+    return results
+

+def test_planes_and_default_writers(geometry) -> None:
+    caches = make_caches(2, 0)
+    caches["model.layers.78.self_attn.indexer.k_cache"] = caches.pop(
+        "model.layers.1.self_attn.indexer.k_cache"
+    )
+    hygiene = Glm53KvHygiene.from_caches(caches, geometry, rank=4, block_size=BLOCK)
+    assert sorted(hygiene.planes) == [
+        (0, "index_key"),
+        (0, "index_scale"),
+        (0, "latent"),
+        (0, "rope"),
+        (1, "latent"),
+        (1, "rope"),
+        (78, "index_key"),
+        (78, "index_scale"),
+    ]
+    # Layer 78 is the drafter's: written on every rank.
+    assert hygiene.transfers == ((0, ((0, "index_key"), (0, "index_scale"))),)
+    # The scale plane sits after the block's 64 keys.
+    rows = Rows.of_positions([3], 5, 6, block_size=BLOCK, device="cpu")
+    cache = caches["model.layers.0.self_attn.indexer.k_cache"]
+    raw = torch.as_strided(cache, (BLOCKS, BLOCK * 132), (cache.stride(0), 1))
+    assert torch.equal(

+        raw[3, BLOCK * 128 + 20 : BLOCK * 128 + 24],

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("table", ["list", "device row"])
+def test_release_completes_the_index_keys(table: str, geometry) -> None:
+    blocks = [4, 1, 3]
+    ids = (
+        blocks if table == "list" else torch.tensor([*blocks, 0, 0], dtype=torch.int32)
+    )
+
+    def work(rank: int, group: Group) -> dict:
+        caches = make_caches(2, 7)  # identical on every rank ...
+        hygiene = Glm53KvHygiene.from_caches(
+            caches, geometry, rank=rank, block_size=BLOCK
+        )
+        if rank in (
+            0,
+            1,
+            2,
+        ):  # ... except the selector ranks' index keys of positions [70, 140)
+            rows = Rows.of_positions(blocks, 70, 140, block_size=BLOCK, device="cpu")
+            for key in ((0, "index_key"), (1, "index_scale")):
+                plane = hygiene.planes[key]
+                rows.scatter(plane, torch.full((70, plane.width), 9, dtype=torch.uint8))
+        snapshot = {name: cache.clone() for name, cache in caches.items()}
+        hygiene.pending.decoded("r", 60, 150)
+        hygiene.release("r", ids, group)
+        return {name: (snapshot[name], cache) for name, cache in caches.items()}
+
+    results = run_ranks(work)
+    for rank, caches in enumerate(results):
+        for name, (old, new) in caches.items():
+            if rank < 3 or name.endswith(".attn"):
+                assert torch.equal(old, new), (rank, name)
+            else:  # the index keys differed from rank 0's before the release
+                assert not torch.equal(old, results[0][name][0]), (rank, name)
+            assert torch.equal(new, results[0][name][1]), (rank, name)

+"""GPU tests of the locality-domain pools (``vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.locality``)."""

+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def domains():
+    from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.locality import domains_for
+
+    try:
+        yield domains_for(torch.device("cuda", 0))
+    except RuntimeError as error:
+        pytest.skip(str(error))
+

+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def geometry():
+    """GLM-5.3's geometry on TP8 (from the package conftest, which a bare run skips)."""
+    import importlib.util
+    from pathlib import Path
+    from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+    from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.ops.launch import Glm53Geometry
+
+    path = Path(__file__).with_name("conftest.py")
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("glm53_test_conftest", path)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return Glm53Geometry.from_config(SimpleNamespace(**module.GLM53_CONFIG), world=8)

+
+def _ordinal(address: int) -> int:
+    from cuda.bindings import driver
+
+    attribute = driver.CUpointer_attribute.CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN_ORDINAL
+    status, value = driver.cuPointerGetAttribute(attribute, address)
+    assert status == driver.CUresult.CUDA_SUCCESS
+    return int(value)
+
+
+def test_sm_table_covers_both_domains(domains) -> None:
+    table = domains.sm_domain
+    assert len(table) == torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).multi_processor_count
+    assert all(table.count(domain) > 0 for domain in range(domains.count))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("domain", [0, 1])
+def test_words_are_homed_and_zeroed(domains, domain: int) -> None:
+    words = domains.words(domain, 1000)
+    assert _ordinal(words.data_ptr()) == domain
+    assert not bool(words.any())
+    words.fill_(3)
+    assert int(words.sum()) == 3000

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""The locality placement degrades to plain memory where the domains are missing."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest

+

+
+SUCCESS = "success"
+
+
+def _driver(count: int = 2, **missing: bool) -> SimpleNamespace:
+    enums = {
+        "CUdevice_attribute": "CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN_COUNT",
+        "CUmemLocationType": "CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN",
+        "CUdevSmResourceGroup_flags": "CU_DEV_SM_RESOURCE_GROUP_LOCALITY_DOMAIN_ID",
+        "CUpointer_attribute": "CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN_ORDINAL",
+    }
+    fields = {
+        enum: SimpleNamespace(**({} if missing.get(enum) else {member: 1}))
+        for enum, member in enums.items()
+    }
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        **fields,
+        CUresult=SimpleNamespace(CUDA_SUCCESS=SUCCESS),
+        cuDevSmResourceSplit=None,
+        cuGreenCtxCreate=None,
+        cuDeviceGetAttribute=lambda attribute, device: (SUCCESS, count),
+    )
+
+
+def test_detection_accepts_two_domains() -> None:
+    assert locality.unsupported_reason(_driver(), 0) == (None, 2)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "enum",
+    [
+        "CUdevice_attribute",
+        "CUmemLocationType",
+        "CUdevSmResourceGroup_flags",
+        "CUpointer_attribute",
+    ],
+)
+def test_detection_reports_a_missing_enum(enum: str) -> None:
+    reason, _ = locality.unsupported_reason(_driver(**{enum: True}), 0)
+    assert reason is not None and enum in reason
+
+
+def test_detection_reports_old_bindings_without_the_calls() -> None:
+    driver = _driver()
+    del driver.cuGreenCtxCreate
+    reason, _ = locality.unsupported_reason(driver, 0)
+    assert reason is not None and "cuGreenCtxCreate" in reason
+
+
+def test_detection_reports_one_domain_and_a_failing_query() -> None:
+    reason, count = locality.unsupported_reason(_driver(count=1), 0)
+    assert reason is not None and count == 1
+    failing = _driver()
+    failing.cuDeviceGetAttribute = lambda attribute, device: ("error", 0)
+    assert locality.unsupported_reason(failing, 0)[0] is not None
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def fallback(monkeypatch):
+    """A :class:`LocalityDomains` on device 0 whose bindings lack the domain enum, and
+    the info lines it logged.
+    """
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("needs a GPU")
+    from cuda.bindings import driver
+
+    lines: list[str] = []
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        locality.logger, "info", lambda message, *args: lines.append(message % args)
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(driver, "CUdevice_attribute", SimpleNamespace())
+    domains = locality.LocalityDomains(torch.device("cuda", 0))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(locality, "_BY_DEVICE", {0: domains})
+    yield domains, lines
+    domains.close()
+
+
+def test_fallback_is_chosen_and_logged_once(fallback) -> None:
+    domains, lines = fallback
+    assert not domains.active
+    assert set(domains.sm_domain) == {0}
+    assert len(domains.sm_domain) == domains.sms
+    assert len(lines) == 1 and "placement off" in lines[0]
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("by_sm", [False, True])
+def test_fallback_keeps_sizes_and_layouts(fallback, by_sm: bool) -> None:
+    from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.arena import Glm53Placement
+    from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.ops.cute_dsl.fused_moe import Flag
+    from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.ops.launch import sizes_of
+
+    placement = Glm53Placement(torch.device("cuda", 0))
+    worker = placement.worker_handoff(by_sm)
+    assert worker.handoff.numel() == worker.mirror.numel() == Handoff.WORDS
+    assert worker.mirror.data_ptr() == worker.handoff.data_ptr() + 4 * Handoff.MIRROR
+    table = worker.handoff[Handoff.ROLE_TABLE : Handoff.ROLE_TABLE + MlaWorker.GRID]
+    assert table.tolist() == list(range(MlaWorker.GRID))
+    flags, mirror = placement.moe_flags()
+    words = sizes_of("fused_moe_q4_ckpt_shared")["kFlagWords"]
+    assert flags.numel() == mirror.numel() == words
+    assert mirror.data_ptr() == flags.data_ptr() + 4 * Flag.MIRROR
+    sm_table = flags[Flag.SM_DOMAIN : Flag.SM_DOMAIN + len(placement.domains.sm_domain)]
+    assert not bool(sm_table.any())
+    worker.mirror.fill_(3)
+    assert int(worker.mirror.sum()) == 3 * Handoff.WORDS
+    placement.release()

+"""Host side of the decode segment at an MTP depth K whose 1 + K tokens do not fill the
+kernels' row groups of four.

+

+

+BLOCK = 64
+
+
+def _tier(rows: int, tokens: int, tokens_buffer: torch.Tensor, hidden=None, **kw):
+    segment = SimpleNamespace(geometry=SimpleNamespace(rows=rows))
+    tensors = {"token_ids": tokens_buffer}
+    if hidden is not None:
+        tensors["segment.hidden"] = hidden
+    return TierState(segment, tensors, None, None, 1, 2, tokens=tokens, **kw)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("live", "padded"),
+    [(1, [7, 7, 7, 7]), (2, [7, 8, 8, 8]), (3, [7, 8, 9, 9]), (4, [7, 8, 9, 10])],
+)
+def test_a_lone_request_repeats_its_last_token_in_its_dead_rows(live, padded):
+    buffer = torch.tensor([7, 8, 9, 10], dtype=torch.int32)
+    hidden = torch.arange(4 * 2, dtype=torch.bfloat16).view(4, 2)
+    tier = _tier(4, live, buffer, hidden)
+    tier.stage_inputs()
+    assert buffer.tolist() == padded
+    assert torch.equal(tier.output(), hidden[:live])
+
+
+def test_a_packed_tier_stages_nothing_and_returns_vllms_rows():
+    buffer = torch.arange(7, 23, dtype=torch.int32)
+    hidden = torch.arange(16 * 2, dtype=torch.bfloat16).view(16, 2)
+    tier = _tier(16, 6, buffer, hidden, packed=True)  # three requests of K = 1
+    tier.stage_inputs()
+    assert buffer.tolist() == list(range(7, 23))
+    assert torch.equal(tier.output(), hidden[:6])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("position", "rows", "live", "zeroed"),
+    [
+        (BLOCK - 1, 4, 1, True),  # MTP off: rows 1..3 are in the next block
+        (BLOCK - 1, 4, 2, False),  # K = 1: row 1 is real and needs the next block
+        (BLOCK - 3, 4, 2, True),  # K = 1: the dead row at p+3 starts the next block
+        (BLOCK - 2, 8, 5, False),  # K = 4: the live rows already end in it
+        (2 * BLOCK - 6, 8, 5, True),  # K = 4: the dead rows p+5..p+7 start a block
+    ],
+)
+def test_only_the_block_past_the_live_rows_is_nulled(position, rows, live, zeroed):
+    table = torch.arange(1, 9, dtype=torch.int32) * 100
+    null_padding_block(table, position, rows, BLOCK, live)
+    nulled = [i for i, entry in enumerate(table.tolist()) if entry == 0]
+    expected = [(position + rows - 1) // BLOCK] if zeroed else []
+    assert nulled == expected

+        row_tiers=True,

+    decode.step(["a", "b"], [10, 10], [2, 2], 4)  # B = 2 at K = 1: packed, q4 MoE
+    decode.step(["a", "b"], [12, 12], [2, 1], 4)  # not a uniform decode step
+    decode.step(["a", "b", "c", "d"], [10] * 4, [2] * 4, 16)  # claimed (no tier built)

+def test_the_host_writes_the_true_rows_and_leaves_the_replay_counter(geometry):

+    layout = RowTableLayout(shaped.rows, shaped.table_requests)

+    assert [table.tensor[layout.context_word(b)].item() for b in range(3)] == [

+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("per_request", "packed"),

+def test_the_ledger_covers_what_a_step_writes(per_request, packed):

+    lone = switch.lone_rows(per_request)
+    stop = ledger_stop(100, per_request, 0, 0 if packed else lone - per_request)
+    assert stop == 100 + (per_request if packed else lone)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""The optional decode-segment hook of Glm53Model.forward."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.nvidia import model as deepseek_v32_model
+from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia import model as glm53_model
+
+
+class _StockPath(Exception):
+    """Raised where the stock forward starts (the pipeline-group lookup)."""
+
+
+class _Segment:
+    def __init__(self, result: torch.Tensor | None) -> None:
+        self.result = result
+        self.calls: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = []
+
+    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, positions: torch.Tensor):
+        self.calls.append((input_ids, positions))
+        return self.result
+
+
+class _Layers(nn.Module):
+    def __iter__(self):
+        raise AssertionError("a claimed forward must not run the layers")
+
+
+def _model(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> glm53_model.Glm53Model:
+    model = object.__new__(glm53_model.Glm53Model)
+    nn.Module.__init__(model)
+    model.norm = nn.Identity()
+    model.layers = _Layers()
+
+    def stock_path():
+        raise _StockPath
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(deepseek_v32_model, "get_pp_group", stock_path)
+    return model
+
+
+def test_no_segment_is_the_default_and_runs_stock(monkeypatch):
+    assert glm53_model.Glm53Model.glm53_segment is None
+    model = _model(monkeypatch)
+    with pytest.raises(_StockPath):
+        model(torch.zeros(4, dtype=torch.int32), torch.arange(4))
+
+
+def test_declining_segment_runs_stock(monkeypatch):
+    model = _model(monkeypatch)
+    segment = _Segment(None)
+    model.glm53_segment = segment
+    input_ids, positions = torch.zeros(4, dtype=torch.int32), torch.arange(4)
+    with pytest.raises(_StockPath):
+        model(input_ids, positions)
+    assert len(segment.calls) == 1 and segment.calls[0][0] is input_ids
+
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Every decode shape (MTP depth K, request count B) is claimed by exactly one path."""
+
+import pytest
+import regex as re
+
+from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia import switch
+from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.switch import ShapePath
+
+MAX_B = 17  # one past the request capacity: always vLLM's stock forward
+
+TABLE = {
+    0: "Q4 P8q4 P8q4 P8q4 P8q8 P8q8 P8q8 P8q8",
+    1: "Q4 P8q4 P8q8 P8q8 P16 P16 P16 P16",
+    2: "Q4 P8q8 P16 P16 P16 S S S",
+    3: "Q4 A8 A16 A16 S S S S",
+    4: "L8 P16 P16 S S S S S",
+    5: "L8 P16 S S S S S S",
+    6: "L8 P16 S S S S S S",
+    7: "L8 A16 S S S S S S",
+}
+CODES = {
+    ShapePath.Q4: "Q4",
+    ShapePath.LONE8: "L8",
+    ShapePath.ALIGNED: "A",
+    ShapePath.PACK: "P",
+    ShapePath.STOCK: "S",
+}
+
+
+def cell(requests: int, drafts: int) -> str:
+    """The table cell of a shape: the path's code, then its tier when it runs on one."""
+    per_request = 1 + drafts
+    path = switch.shape_path(requests, per_request)
+    code = CODES[path]
+    if path in (ShapePath.ALIGNED, ShapePath.PACK):
+        w8a16 = switch.shape_w8a16_rows(requests, per_request)
+        moe = f"q{w8a16}" if w8a16 else ""
+        return f"{code}{switch.shape_tier(requests, per_request)}{moe}"
+    return code
+
+
+def shapes():
+    """Every (K, B) of K = 0..7 and B = 1..17."""
+    return [(k, b) for k in range(8) for b in range(1, MAX_B + 1)]
+
+
+def test_the_claim_function_gives_the_table():
+    found = {k: " ".join(cell(b, k) for b in range(1, 9)) for k in range(8)}
+    assert found == TABLE
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("drafts", "requests"), shapes())
+def test_a_shape_has_one_path_and_the_arithmetic_agrees(drafts, requests):
+    per_request = 1 + drafts
+    rows = requests * per_request
+    path = switch.shape_path(requests, per_request)
+    assert isinstance(path, ShapePath)
+    stock = requests > 16 or rows > 16
+    assert (path is ShapePath.STOCK) == stock
+    assert switch.serves_shape(requests, per_request) == (not stock)
+    assert switch.shape_w8a16_rows(requests, per_request) == (
+        (4 if rows <= 4 else 8) if path is ShapePath.PACK and rows <= 8 else 0
+    )
+    assert (path is ShapePath.Q4) == (requests == 1 and per_request <= 4)
+    assert (path is ShapePath.LONE8) == (requests == 1 and per_request > 4)
+    assert (path is ShapePath.ALIGNED) == (
+        requests >= 2 and per_request % 4 == 0 and not stock
+    )
+    assert (path is ShapePath.PACK) == (
+        requests >= 2 and per_request % 4 != 0 and not stock
+    )
+    # --max-num-seqs = B: the graphs claim the served counts, stock steps none.
+    served = switch.served_requests(requests, per_request)
+    assert (served < requests) == stock
+    found = switch.graphs(requests, per_request)
+    claimed = {b for graph in found for b in graph.requests}
+    assert claimed == set(range(1, served + 1))
+    assert switch.derived_tiers(requests, per_request)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("drafts", "requests"), shapes())
+def test_the_tier_and_the_entry_names_follow_the_claim(drafts, requests, geometry):
+    per_request = 1 + drafts
+    path = switch.shape_path(requests, per_request)
+    if path is ShapePath.STOCK:
+        return
+    tier = switch.shape_tier(requests, per_request)
+    rows = requests * per_request
+    packed = switch.packed_tier(tier, per_request)
+    assert packed == (path is ShapePath.PACK)
+    assert tier >= rows
+    kernel_rows = per_request if packed else switch.lone_rows(per_request)
+    w8a16 = switch.shape_w8a16_rows(requests, per_request)
+    shaped = geometry.for_tier(
+        tier, kernel_rows - 1, packed, w8a16, 0 if packed else per_request
+    )
+    if packed:  # the q4 build (one request) has its own MoE whatever the flag says
+        assert ("fused_moe_q4_" in shaped.moe_kernel(3)) == (w8a16 == 4)
+    assert shaped.max_requests >= requests
+    for layer in (3, 4):
+        uses_q8 = shaped.moe_kernel(layer).startswith("fused_moe_q8")
+        # The tier-8 builds: K = 3 at B = 2, and a lone request of five to eight rows.
+        lone8 = requests == 1 and drafts >= 4
+        assert uses_q8 == (w8a16 == 8 or (requests, drafts) == (2, 3) or lone8)
+    names = [
+        shaped.selector_kernel(0),
+        shaped.worker_kernel(0, 0),
+        shaped.worker_kernel(1, 0),
+        shaped.prologue_kernel(False),
+    ]
+    for name in names:
+        assert bool(re.search(r"_r\d+p(_|$)", name)) == packed, name
+    for name in (shaped.moe_kernel(3), shaped.dense_kernel):
+        assert not re.search(r"r\d+p", name), name
+    dead_rows = path is ShapePath.LONE8 and per_request < kernel_rows
+    assert bool(re.search(r"d\d+x\d+", shaped.moe_kernel(3))) == dead_rows
+    assert not re.search(r"d\d+x\d+", shaped.dense_kernel), shaped.dense_kernel
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("drafts", "tag"),
+    [(4, "q8d8x5"), (5, "q8d8x6"), (6, "q8d8x7"), (7, "q8")],
+)
+def test_a_lone_request_with_dead_rows_runs_the_masked_moe(geometry, drafts, tag):
+    from vllm.models.glm53.nvidia.ops.cute_dsl import registry
+
+    per_request = drafts + 1
+    assert switch.shape_path(1, per_request) is ShapePath.LONE8
+    kernel_rows = switch.lone_rows(per_request)
+    assert kernel_rows == 8
+    shaped = geometry.for_tier(8, kernel_rows - 1, False, False, per_request)
+    assert shaped.moe_tag == tag
+    for layer in (3, 4):
+        knobs = dict(registry.ENTRIES[shaped.moe_kernel(layer)].constants)
+        dead = (knobs.get("DEAD_STRIDE", 0), knobs.get("DEAD_LIVE", 0))
+        assert dead == ((8, per_request) if per_request < 8 else (0, 0))

+            self_attn=SimpleNamespace(

+                indexer=SimpleNamespace(
+                    k_norm=norm(geometry.index_dim, bias=True),
+                    wk_weights_proj=SimpleNamespace(

+                            data=torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16)

+                ),

+    return SimpleNamespace(layers=[layer(), layer(), layer(), layer()])

+def _stash(geometry, rank: int, narrow: bool, wide: bool) -> weights.CheckpointStash:
+    g, world_heads = geometry, geometry.heads * WORLD
+    stash = weights.CheckpointStash(g, rank, torch.device("cpu"), narrow, wide)
+    stash._kept[(0, "self_attn.q_b_proj.weight_scale_inv")] = torch.ones(
+        world_heads * g.qk_head // g.block, g.q_lora // g.block
+    )
+    stash._kept[(0, "self_attn.kv_b_proj.weight_scale_inv")] = torch.ones(
+        world_heads * g.kv_b_stride // g.block, g.kv_lora // g.block
+    )
+    for head in weights.head_groups(g, 0, rank, narrow):
+        stash._kept[(0, f"self_attn.q_b_proj.weight@{head}")] = _fp8(
+            g.heads * g.qk_head, g.q_lora
+        )
+        stash._kept[(0, f"self_attn.kv_b_proj.weight@{head}")] = _fp8(
+            g.heads * g.kv_b_stride, g.kv_lora
+        )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Model Runner V2's low-batch speculative decode paths.
+
+The fused kernels match the sequences they replace bitwise on random batches
+(padded rows, prefill-tail rows): the draft prefill's fused IO and the final
+draft step's store into the runner's table.
+Also the post-forward CUDA graph: its opt-in, per-step conditions and replay.
+"""
+
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import triton
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu import post_forward_cudagraph as pf_module
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils import copy_small
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.input_batch import (
+    InputBuffers,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.post_forward_cudagraph import (
+    PostForwardCudaGraphs,
+    maybe_create_post_forward_cudagraphs,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.states import NO_LOGPROBS
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.target_dependent_ar.speculator import (
+    _draft_prefill_store_kernel,
+    prepare_prefill_inputs,
+    update_draft_inputs,
+)
+
+needs_cuda = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a CUDA device"
+)
+
+K = 3  # speculative tokens
+MAX_REQS = 8
+HIDDEN = 3000
+I64 = torch.int64
+
+
+def _ri(g, lo, hi, shape, dtype=torch.int32):
+    """Random integers in [lo, hi) of ``shape`` (an int or a tuple)."""
+    shape = shape if isinstance(shape, tuple) else (shape,)
+    return torch.randint(lo, hi, shape, generator=g, dtype=dtype)
+
+
+def _map(x, fn):
+    """Apply ``fn`` to every tensor in nested tuples, namespaces and dicts."""
+    if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor):
+        return fn(x)
+    if isinstance(x, tuple):
+        return tuple(_map(v, fn) for v in x)
+    if isinstance(x, SimpleNamespace):
+        return SimpleNamespace(**{k: _map(v, fn) for k, v in vars(x).items()})
+    if isinstance(x, dict):
+        return {k: _map(v, fn) for k, v in x.items()}
+    return x
+
+
+@needs_cuda
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(6))
+def test_draft_prefill_positions_and_row_store(seed: int):
+    """prepare_prefill_inputs also writes each request's sampled-row position
+    and +1 (padded rows: position 0's), and _draft_prefill_store_kernel stores
+    the sampled hidden rows and those positions as the gathers they replace."""
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    dev = torch.device("cuda")
+    num_reqs = int(torch.randint(1, MAX_REQS + 1, (1,), generator=g))
+    num_tokens = num_reqs * (K + 1)
+    batch = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_reqs=num_reqs,
+        idx_mapping=torch.randperm(MAX_REQS, generator=g)[:num_reqs].int(),
+        input_ids=_ri(g, 0, 99, num_tokens),
+        positions=_ri(g, 0, 999, num_tokens, I64),
+        query_start_loc=torch.arange(num_reqs + 1, dtype=torch.int32) * (K + 1),
+        seq_lens=_ri(g, 5, 99, num_reqs),
+    )
+    num_sampled = _ri(g, 1, K + 2, num_reqs)
+    last_sampled = _ri(g, 0, 99, (MAX_REQS, 1), I64)
+    next_prefill = _ri(g, 0, 99, MAX_REQS)
+    src = torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN, generator=g).bfloat16()
+    batch, num_sampled, last_sampled, next_prefill, src = _map(
+        (batch, num_sampled, last_sampled, next_prefill, src), torch.Tensor.cuda
+    )
+    last_token_indices = torch.zeros(MAX_REQS, dtype=I64, device=dev)
+    prefill_positions = torch.full((MAX_REQS,), -7, dtype=I64, device=dev)
+    prefill_sample_src = torch.full_like(prefill_positions, -7)
+    buffers = InputBuffers(MAX_REQS, num_tokens + 4, dev)
+    prepare_prefill_inputs(
+        last_token_indices,
+        torch.zeros((), dtype=I64, device=dev),
+        buffers,
+        batch,
+        num_sampled,
+        K + 1 - num_sampled,
+        last_sampled,
+        next_prefill,
+        MAX_REQS,
+        prefill_positions,
+        prefill_sample_src,
+    )
+    gathered = buffers.positions[last_token_indices]
+    assert torch.equal(prefill_positions, gathered)
+    assert torch.equal(prefill_sample_src, gathered + 1)
+
+    dst = torch.zeros(MAX_REQS, HIDDEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
+    dst_pos, dst_src = torch.zeros(2, MAX_REQS, dtype=I64, device=dev)
+    _draft_prefill_store_kernel[(num_reqs, triton.cdiv(HIDDEN, 1024))](
+        src,
+        src.stride(0),
+        last_token_indices,
+        dst,
+        dst.stride(0),
+        prefill_positions,
+        dst_pos,
+        prefill_sample_src,
+        dst_src,
+        HIDDEN,
+        BLOCK=1024,
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(dst[:num_reqs], src[last_token_indices[:num_reqs]])
+    assert torch.equal(dst_pos[:num_reqs], prefill_positions[:num_reqs])
+    assert torch.equal(dst_src[:num_reqs], prefill_sample_src[:num_reqs])
+

+@needs_cuda
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(4))
+def test_final_draft_step_stores_into_the_sink(seed: int):
+    """update_draft_inputs with a sink: the final step stores each request's
+    drafts into sink[idx_mapping[r]] (the runner's draft-token table) exactly as
+    the runner's store would, and skips rows whose idx_mapping is -1."""
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    dev = torch.device("cuda")
+    num_reqs = int(torch.randint(1, MAX_REQS + 1, (1,), generator=g))
+    hidden = torch.randn(num_reqs, HIDDEN, generator=g).bfloat16().to(dev)
+    output = _ri(g, 0, 99, (MAX_REQS, K), I64).to(dev)
+    sink = torch.full((MAX_REQS, K), -5, dtype=I64, device=dev)
+    idx_mapping = torch.randperm(MAX_REQS, generator=g)[:num_reqs].int().to(dev)
+    if num_reqs > 1:
+        idx_mapping[-1] = -1  # a padded row
+    drafts = _ri(g, 0, 99, num_reqs, I64).to(dev)
+    update_draft_inputs(
+        drafts,
+        torch.full((), K - 1, dtype=I64, device=dev),
+        hidden,
+        output,
+        torch.zeros(MAX_REQS, HIDDEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev),
+        InputBuffers(MAX_REQS, MAX_REQS * (K + 1), dev),
+        torch.zeros(MAX_REQS, dtype=I64, device=dev),
+        num_reqs,
+        1 << 20,
+        K,
+        idx_mapping=idx_mapping,
+        sink=sink,
+    )
+    expected = torch.full_like(sink, -5)
+    for row, target in enumerate(idx_mapping.tolist()):
+        if target >= 0:
+            expected[target] = output[row]
+    assert torch.equal(output[:num_reqs, K - 1], drafts)
+    assert torch.equal(sink, expected)
+

+def fake_cudagraphs(monkeypatch):
+    """Record captures, replays and stream waits in place of CUDA graphs: a
+    capture runs its launches once, eagerly, and a replay runs nothing."""
+    rec = SimpleNamespace(graphs=[], events=[])
+
+    class FakeGraph:
+        def __init__(self):
+            self.replays = 0
+            rec.graphs.append(self)
+
+        def replay(self):
+            self.replays += 1
+            rec.events.append("replay")
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def capture(graph, pool=None, stream=None, capture_error_mode="global"):
+        rec.events.append("capture")
+        yield
+
+    stream = SimpleNamespace(wait_event=lambda e: rec.events.append(("wait", e)))
+    platform = SimpleNamespace(graph_pool_handle=lambda: 0)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "CUDAGraph", FakeGraph)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "graph", capture)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(pf_module, "current_stream", lambda: stream)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(pf_module, "current_platform", platform)
+    return rec

+def test_post_forward_warm_up_capture_replay_and_release(fake_cudagraphs):
+    events = fake_cudagraphs.events
+    graphs = PostForwardCudaGraphs(None, 4, 32, torch.device("cpu"))
+    calls: list = []
+
+    def fn():
+        calls.append(None)
+        return (object(), len(calls))
+
+    assert graphs._run("a", fn)[1] == 1 and not events  # warm-up: eager
+    captured = graphs._run("a", fn)
+    assert events == ["capture", "replay"]
+    graphs.set_output_copy_event("copied")
+    assert graphs._run("a", fn) is captured and len(calls) == 2
+    assert events[2:] == [("wait", "copied"), "replay"]
+    graphs.release()
+    events.clear()
+    graphs._run("a", fn)
+    assert len(calls) == 3 and not events  # warm-up again
+

+            needs_logits_processing=np.zeros(4, dtype=bool),

+        ),
+        speculator=SimpleNamespace(acceptance_estimator=None),

+            uses_prompt_logprobs=np.zeros(4, dtype=bool), token_id_scores={}
+        ),
+    )
+    batch = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_reqs=2,
+        has_prefill=False,
+        has_structured_output_reqs=False,
+        num_draft_tokens=2 * K,
+        num_scheduled_tokens=np.full(2, K + 1, dtype=np.int32),
+        num_tokens=2 * (K + 1),

+def test_post_forward_captured_region_replays_like_eager():
+    """A region reading a persistent input through copy_small (a kernel copy
+    under capture, bitwise, NaN payloads and -0.0 included) replays exactly what
+    the eager region computes as the input changes."""
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    graphs = PostForwardCudaGraphs(None, 4, 32, device)

+    dst = torch.empty_like(src)
+

+        copy_small(dst, src)

+
+    gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(0)
+    with torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.Stream()):
+        for step in range(5):

+            for a, b in zip(got, want):
+                assert torch.equal(a.view(torch.int8), b.view(torch.int8)), step

+# GLM-5.3 latency-specialized decode (NVIDIA)
+
+GLM-5.3 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) serves low-batch decode at low latency on 8xB200
+(SM100) and 8xB300 (SM103): steps of B requests of 1 + K tokens, B (1 + K) <= 16 rows
+(up to 16 requests with MTP off, 4 at MTP K = 3). CuTe DSL kernels (`ops/cute_dsl`)
+replace vLLM's FULL uniform decode graph of the 78 target layers. The MTP drafter
+(layer 78) runs on vLLM's speculator, its decode steps as CuTe DSL kernels too
+(Specialized drafter below). Every other forward (prefill, mixed steps, eager
+steps) stays on vLLM's stock layers.
+
+## Terms
+
+- `q4`, `q8`: the four-row build (one request of up to four rows) and the eight-row
+  W8A16 MoE; entry names carry them (`*_q4*`, `*_q8*`).
+- `seam`: the MoE of a layer whose next layer reuses an earlier layer's index selection;
+  it also writes the next layer's normalized input (`*_seam*` entries).
+- `probe`: the attention worker of a layer with its own index selection, on a rank that
+  also runs the selector; its weight forms are named `probe.*`.
+- `ckpt_shared` (MoE entries): the MoE reads the checkpoint's FP8 experts in place and
+  includes the shared expert.
+
+## Layout
+
+| Module | Role |
+| --- | --- |
+| `model.py` | The DSA decoder and `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with the segment hooks, plus `Glm53ModelState` (Model Runner V2), which tracks requests and steps for the segment. |
+| `switch.py` | Reads `decode_backend` once, in `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM.__init__`, into a frozen `LowLatencyDecode` record; refuses unsupported deployments. |
+| `decode.py` | `SpecializedDecode`, segment 1 (the target layers): build, launch, capture and the model hook. |
+| `weights.py` | The segment's weight forms, built from the checkpoint during load. |
+| `kv.py` | KV-cache hygiene between the segment and vLLM's stock forwards (index-key rank completion). |
+| `arena.py` | The cross-rank peer arena and its placement (plain memory where the optional locality placement is unavailable). |
+| `providers.py` | The segment's launch providers (prologue, selector, worker, FFN): each allocates its results and protocol state, names its peer-mailbox slices and fixes its launch's arguments. |
+| `ops/cute_dsl/` | CuTe DSL kernel families (`registry.py`: served entry to kernel class, host sizes, compiled host wrapper and its object cache; `fused_moe.py` also owns the expert layout). |
+| `ops/launch.py` | `Glm53Geometry`, the model's shapes and layer layout read from the config, and binding and running the compiled launches. |
+
+The model class (`model.py`) owns the hooks: the target model's
+forward offers each step to the installed segment, and `process_weights_after_loading`
+builds the weight forms and installs the segment.
+Runner-side hooks that are not model-specific stay in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/`.
+
+## Switch
+
+`--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'` turns on the
+whole path, as Kimi K3's specialized decode does: the kernels, the weight forms,
+segment 1 and the drafter segment (`auto`, the default, keeps vLLM's decode). With
+the path on, startup refuses, on every TP rank (a MIN all-reduce over the TP group),
+unless: the GPU is SM100 or SM103; tensor parallel size is 8 without pipeline
+parallelism; the KV cache is FlashInfer MLA's 576-byte fp8 rows
+(`--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8`, vLLM's SM10x
+default); the segment runs under Model Runner V2; decode steps run in FULL CUDA graphs
+(not `--enforce-eager`); MTP, if configured, sets `use_local_argmax_reduction`.
+
+## Deployment
+
+Set a persistent `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` (node-local, reused across restarts). It holds
+the compiled CuTe host wrappers (`glm53_kernels/<entry>.<arch>.<key>.o`; a cold build is about 40 s per rank) and
+DeepGEMM's JIT cache (`deep_gemm`, for the dense FP8 linears). A cold
+node also needs `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600`, past vLLM's default 600 s.
+The model state opts in to Model Runner V2's low-latency decode paths
+(`ModelState.low_latency_decode`); with MTP, the sampling, state update and
+draft-prefill inputs after each uniform decode step then run as one CUDA graph.
+
+```bash
+export VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/local/ssd/vllm-cache VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
+vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --block-size 64 \
+  --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+  --max-num-seqs 16 \
+  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
+  --additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'
+```
+
+- With MTP, add `--speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
+  "use_local_argmax_reduction": true}'` and `--max-num-seqs 4` (K = 3: four rows per
+  request). The drafter is vLLM's MTP; `use_local_argmax_reduction` takes its greedy drafts
+  from a per-rank argmax (the switch requires it with MTP). Benchmarks at a fixed
+  acceptance length add vLLM's synthetic acceptance:
+  `"rejection_sample_method": "synthetic", "synthetic_acceptance_length": 2.99`.
+- The path serves the MoE from vLLM's `flashinfer_trtllm` experts (FlashInfer trtllm-gen's
+  DeepSeekFp8 BlockMajorK form, stock's default on SM100), which the decode MoE kernels
+  read in place (`fused_moe.LAYOUT`): vLLM's routed and shared expert tensors and its FP32
+  routed scales stay where vLLM allocated them, and the segment adds only a 1152-byte header
+  per layer (the shared expert's scales decoded to FP32). `--moe-backend`
+  is not needed: the switch turns vLLM's `auto` into `flashinfer_trtllm` and refuses any
+  other explicit backend, and vLLM's MTP drafter inherits it. The steps vLLM's stock
+  forward runs (Batch shapes) read the same experts with stock's kernels.
+- Without `--speculative-config` (MTP off) the segment claims vLLM's one-token
+  decode graphs. One request runs as a T = 4 step: rows 1-3 repeat the token at
+  p+1..p+3 as padding, vLLM's head samples row 0, and padding rows past p's block
+  write vLLM's null block. Several requests run packed (Batch shapes).
+- The KV pool needs no `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`: the segments built during
+  vLLM's CUDA graph memory profiling are rebuilt over the pool vLLM binds after it.
+- The startup log shows `GLM-5.3 latency-specialized decode: MTP K=1: B = [1]: the q4
+  build; B = [2]: packed rows on tier 8 (q4 MoE, at most 4 live rows); B = [3, 4]:
+  packed rows on tier 8 (q8 MoE, at most 8 live rows)` (one clause per CUDA graph;
+  `--max-num-seqs 4` at K = 1) and `GLM-5.3 segment 1 installed (row tiers [4, 8, 16],
+  claims [2, 4, 8, 16]-token forwards)`
+  (K = 1, `--max-num-seqs` 8: the row tiers and the forward sizes the segment claims).
+
+## Batch shapes
+
+`switch.shape_path` claims every (MTP K, B requests) shape exactly once; the build, its
+kernels, the CUDA graph sizes (one graph per run of request counts on the same build,
+derived when `--cudagraph-capture-sizes` is left out) and the steps left to vLLM's stock
+forward all follow from it. A request owns `1 + K` contiguous rows; a step has
+`R = B (1 + K)` live rows.
+
+| K | B = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9-16 |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 0 | Q4 | P8q4 | P8q4 | P8q4 | P8q8 | P8q8 | P8q8 | P8q8 | P16 |
+| 1 | Q4 | P8q4 | P8q8 | P8q8 | P16 | P16 | P16 | P16 | S |
+| 2 | Q4 | P8q8 | P16 | P16 | P16 | S | S | S | S |
+| 3 | Q4 | A8 | A16 | A16 | S | S | S | S | S |
+| 4 | L8 | P16 | P16 | S | S | S | S | S | S |
+| 5 | L8 | P16 | S | S | S | S | S | S | S |
+| 6 | L8 | P16 | S | S | S | S | S | S | S |
+| 7 | L8 | A16 | S | S | S | S | S | S | S |
+
+- `Q4`: one request of at most four rows on the one-request build (four rows). Its
+  tokens come first, then dead rows that repeat the last token at the next positions;
+  nothing reads their results.
+- `L8`: one request of five to eight rows on the 8-row build, with the same dead rows
+  below eight rows (K = 4 to 6). Its two row groups select in parallel, rank g for group g
+  (the second group's rank first inserts the first group's new index keys); every rank
+  then holds all ids, as in the request-parallel tiers.
+- `A<n>`: several requests of a whole number of row groups (K = 3, 7) on tier `n`, the
+  smallest that holds `R`; no dead rows.
+- `P<n>`: packed rows on tier `n` (8 or 16, the smallest that holds `R` and a selector
+  slot per segment: tier 8 has eight slots, tier 16 sixteen): the true rows of all
+  requests lie back to back with no dead rows, a group of four rows may hold several
+  requests, and the index selection runs one segment of at most four rows of one request
+  per slot, request-parallel over all eight ranks (rank `r` serves requests `r` and
+  `r + 8`).
+- `S`: vLLM's stock forward, in the same deployment. The segment's steps hold at most
+  16 requests and `R = B (1 + K) <= 16` rows (16 requests for K = 0, 8 for K = 1, 5 at K = 2,
+  4 at K = 3, 3 at K = 4, and 2 at K = 5 to 7); any `--max-num-seqs` starts, and a
+  larger step replays vLLM's own CUDA graph: the capture sizes keep vLLM's sizes above
+  the segment's largest graph, up to `--max-num-seqs` x (1 + K). Before such a step the
+  step hook completes the index keys the segment wrote on the selector ranks only (a
+  replay skips the forward hook). No tier above 16 rows is built. Every prefill or
+  mixed step runs vLLM's path. The log names each step size once: `GLM-5.3 uniform
+  decode steps: 41, vLLM's stock forward 12 (this step: 32 tokens, stock)` (or
+  `tier 16`). The stock forward's MoE runs stock's `flashinfer_trtllm` kernels on the
+  same experts, as stock vLLM's `auto` backend does.
+  The stock graphs of steps above the tiers take more memory than vLLM's CUDA graph
+  estimate (B200 TP8, `--gpu-memory-utilization` 0.92: 4.44 vs 0.93 GiB at K = 3 and
+  `--max-num-seqs` 16, 7.28 vs 0.69 GiB at K = 1), leaving about 6.5 GiB free per GPU.
+
+The row tiers are 8 and 16 plus the one-request build of four rows.
+
+Precision. A step of at most eight live rows runs a W8A16 MoE: the one-request build's
+four-row MoE for every `Q4` step and the packed `P8q4` steps (at most four rows), the
+eight-row `q8` MoE for the packed `P8q8` steps (five to eight rows), for `A8` (K = 3,
+B = 2) and for every `L8` step, seam layers included. A `P8q4` / `P8q8` step runs tier 8
+with one / two live row groups and its MoE on rows 0..3 / 0..7 of the hidden buffer;
+tail rows past `R` reach the MoE with stale data and their results are not read. The q8
+MoE routes only its live rows (the row table's `R`; for `L8` at K = 4 to 6 the request's
+`1 + K` tokens, entries `q8d8x<live>`): rows past them add no expert to the union. Every
+step of nine or more live rows uses the batched W8A8 MoE.
+K >= 4 multi-group requests are not bitwise reproducible run to run, because the
+accumulation order is free.
+
+Device memory per rank at the largest `--max-num-seqs` (MiB; peer arena, results and
+protocol state of every build of the deployment, from the build plans):
+
+| K | `--max-num-seqs` | MiB |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 0 | 16 | 5724 |
+| 1 | 8 | 5724 |
+| 2 | 5 | 4444 |
+| 3 | 4 | 2836 |
+| 4 | 3 | 3490 |
+| 5 | 2 | 3490 |
+| 6 | 2 | 3490 |
+| 7 | 2 | 2423 |
+
+The segment allocates this at startup, so at a fixed memory budget every MiB is a MiB
+less KV pool. The packed tier-16 build is shared by every K and its selector has 16
+slots (K = 0 at B = 16 needs them), 2662 MiB of the totals; K >= 1 fills at most eight. K = 0 and 1 keep two builds on tier 8 (the q4 MoE and the q8 MoE), each
+with its own arena.
+
+## Specialized drafter
+
+With `latency_specialized` the MTP drafter (layer 78) also runs as CuTe DSL kernels.
+The target model registers `GlmMoeDsaMTP` (`mtp.py`, vLLM's DeepSeek-V3.2 MTP model with
+the drafter hooks) under the `DeepseekV32MTPModel` architecture before vLLM builds the
+drafter; without the switch vLLM's stock drafter runs. Per decode step the drafter runs a
+catch-up over the step's rows (vLLM's draft prefill) and one proposal per later draft. It
+serves MTP K = 1..7 (`switch.DRAFT_KS`): the catch-up kernels hold four rows a request, so
+at K = 4..7 (T = 5..8 rows) the catch-up runs twice in the same graph, over rows 0..3 and
+the last four. The other window runs first, up to its worker, and only writes its rows'
+latents and index keys; the window with the accepted row (the low one when both hold it)
+runs the whole catch-up. At K = 1, 2 (T = 2, 3) one window is padded to four rows, as the
+target pads a lone request: the dead rows repeat row T - 1 and write latents and index keys
+only past the step's tokens, beyond what the accepted row reads (the next step's rows
+overwrite them before any row reads them). vLLM reserves slots through p + 2K, so at K = 1
+the last dead row may fall in an unreserved block, whose block-table entry the staging
+kernel points at the null block for that step (vLLM gathers every reserved entry of the
+row again before the next step, so a nulled entry never outlives it). K = 1 has no
+proposal. The modules:
+
+| Module | Role |
+| --- | --- |
+| `mtp.py` | `GlmMoeDsaMTP`, the drafter model with the hooks, and its registration. |
+| `draft.py` | The drafter segment: hook, graphs, rebuild after a KV-cache rebind, warm-up, and weight forms (layer 78 bound in place to vLLM's tensors). |
+| `draft_providers.py` | The drafter's launch providers (`providers.Provider`): results, protocol state and peer-arena slices, bound and run like segment 1's. |
+| `ops/cute_dsl/mla_draft.py` | `DraftWorker`: the layer-78 worker over vLLM's eight heads of each rank (four rows for the catch-up, one for a proposal). |
+| `ops/cute_dsl/mtp_preprocess.py` | The MTP preprocess (`enorm`, `hnorm`, `eh_proj`). |
+| `ops/cute_dsl/lm_head.py` | The BF16 draft head `lm_head_top1_q1`: final RMSNorm, the rank's vocabulary-shard logits and their top-1. |
+
+The catch-up's selection runs the only-row selector shards (`SelectorOnlyRow`, ranks 0-2)
+before the worker; every rank runs the worker in both parts. The worker writes its attended
+row four times, and the MoE is the target's `fused_moe_q4_ckpt_shared`; the BF16 draft head
+(`lm_head_top1_q1`) reads row 0.
+
+Request tiers. At MTP 3 the drafter serves steps of up to four requests: it builds the
+tiers of 1, 2 and 4 requests that `--max-num-seqs` allows
+(`switch.draft_tiers`) and a step runs the smallest tier that holds its requests; the groups
+past the step's requests are
+skipped. A tier is the one-request kernels run over request groups: the catch-up has four rows a
+request, a proposal one, and the selector and the worker loop over the request groups inside one
+launch each (`RowGroups`, the target's row tiers' mechanism) while the preprocess, the MoE and the
+head run once per four requests. Each tier is one catch-up graph and one draft-decode graph that
+vLLM captures at the tier's size, so the capture sizes are the row tiers plus 1 and 2
+(`switch.draft_capture_sizes`). The row tables and the per-request step words (position, accepted
+row, context length, selection generation) are written each step by the model state's
+preprocess hook and by two small kernels in the captured graphs. A request's results are bitwise
+those of the one-request build except the MoE, which sums its experts over the rows of its launch,
+and the head, whose four-row build reduces in another order (relative RMS below 5e-3).
+A drafter tier is the top request count of one of the target's graphs, whose rows its
+catch-up replays at (`switch.draft_tiers`): four requests at MTP 3, two at MTP 1 (three and
+four ran 1.3 % slower a step than vLLM's drafter), at MTP 2 four
+while `--max-num-seqs` is at most 4 (from five on, three to five requests share the
+15-token graph: two), two at MTP 5 to 7, and at MTP 4 two only while `--max-num-seqs` is
+2 (from three on, two requests pad to the three-request graph). A
+drafter tier binds the block table of the target build its catch-up replays at (at MTP 1
+tier 8 has two: two requests on the q4 MoE build, three or four on the q8 one). Any other step runs vLLM's drafter, at any `--max-num-seqs`.
+vLLM's draft decode graphs are captured only at sizes up to `--max-num-seqs` (one token a
+request), which the row tiers' token counts are not, so the capture sizes also hold the
+request counts 1, 2, 4, 8 and `--max-num-seqs` itself unless one would split a run of the
+target's graphs (same function; at K = 3 and `--max-num-seqs` 13 to 15, draft decodes of
+9 or more requests then run eagerly); without them a draft decode of fewer requests than
+the smallest row graph ran eagerly (all of them at K = 4 to 7). The catch-up writes the drafter
+layer's index keys on the selector ranks only; before the first step vLLM's drafter serves after
+CuTe steps, the pending rows are completed on every rank (by the admitting prefill step's eager
+forward, or by the target's step hook when the admission replays as a decode).
+
+The drafter reads layer 78 as stock vLLM loads it for the shipped checkpoint: the worker's
+`fused_qkv_a`, `q_b`, `kv_b` and `o_proj` and the selector's `indexer.wq_b` are E4M3 with
+DeepGEMM UE8M0 scales, moved once into `VllmLinear` buffers like the target's; the routed
+experts and the shared expert are read in place, as in the target layers; `eh_proj` (read through a TMA map), `wk_weights_proj`, the router, the norms, the
+embedding and the head are BF16 as loaded; the KV cache is vLLM's FP8 cache. Activations are
+BF16 with FP32 accumulation.
+The startup log shows `GLM-5.3 drafter segment installed (T = 4, 2 proposals)`, and after
+the first eager draft prefill `GLM-5.3 drafter segment built`.
